facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: The sea, which had been beating against the shores, suddenly broke the boundary that was imposed on it by nature... The sea covered up everything in the city.
facts.text: In the Mausala Parva of the Mahabharata, the ocean breaches its natural bounds to engulf the entire city of Dvaraka immediately as Arjuna departs with the surviving citizens.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: The ocean gave twelve yojanas of land to Krishna where Dvaravati was built.
facts.text: The Harivamsa states that Krishna directed the divine architect Vishvakarma to build the coastal city of Dvaravati on land reclaimed after requesting space from the sea.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The typology of anchors has indicated that Dwarka was an important port since historical period.
facts.text: Marine archaeologists from the National Institute of Oceanography identified multiple varieties of stone anchors, including triangular composite anchors and Indo-Arab grapnel anchors, in Dwarka waters.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Two Bronze Age stone-anchors, an Indus type seal, an inscribed jar, a coppersmith's stone mould, iron and shell objects and post-Harappan pottery are among the datable finds from the excavation.
facts.text: Excavations conducted by marine archaeologists at nearby Bet Dwarka island yielded Late Harappan seals, inscribed protohistoric pottery, and copper artifacts.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Based on explorations, underwater excavations were carried out in 2007. The objective of the excavation was to know the antiquity of the site, based on material evidence.
facts.text: The Underwater Archaeology Wing of the Archaeological Survey of India carried out offshore excavations off Dwarka in 2007 to document submerged circular structures and verify the antiquity of the remains.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: In all, eight settlements can be distinguished at Dwarka. The first settlement made in the 15th century B.C. was submerged or washed away.
facts.text: Onshore archaeological excavations at the Dwarkadhish Temple complex revealed evidence of eight successive settlement phases dating from antiquity through the medieval period.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: At present the data indicate possible dates for these anchors of between the 2nd century BC and 10th century AD.
facts.text: S.R. Rao dated the submerged stone remains to approximately 1500 BCE, whereas subsequent NIO archaeologists dated the stone anchors and harbor works between the 2nd century BCE and the 14th century CE.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Offshore explorations have brought to light a large number of stone structures, which appear to be the remains of an ancient jetty.
facts.text: While early excavators interpreted the offshore stone alignments as the defensive bastions of a submerged city, later marine archaeologists argued they represent the collapsed remnants of an ancient harbor jetty and wharf.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Coastal erosion, sea-level changes, and repeated rebuilding over centuries make the site's history incredibly complex.
facts.text: Some researchers propose the coastal structures were submerged suddenly by a catastrophic palaeo-tsunami, whereas marine geologists argue the inundation was the result of gradual coastal erosion and Holocene sea-level fluctuations.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: According to popular local belief, the magnificent golden palaces of Krishna remained intact beneath the deep sea.
facts.text: Popular regional folklore asserts that an entire city composed of golden palaces and intact towers remains preserved on the deep seafloor off the coast of Dwarka.
